info.name: Korsi Live Meeting Bridge
info.summary: Sends the transcript of Talk calls in Korsi-linked rooms to Korsi for live analysis.
info.description:
A fork of Nextcloud's Live Transcription app, rebuilt as a bridge to Korsi.
What it does: Korsi tells this app which Talk conversations belong to an operational case. When a call starts in one of them, the app joins, mixes the participants' audio into one stream, transcribes it through Korsi's speech provider under a temporary key Korsi issues for that call, and posts the resulting **text** back to Korsi every few minutes. Korsi analyses it and shows a live reading of the meeting in its own interface.
What it does not do: it shows nothing in Talk, and it has no captions button. There is no per-meeting opt-in — a call in a linked room is read, which is the point for organizations that expect their meetings to be on the record.
Audio never reaches Korsi's servers. It goes from this container straight to the speech provider.
Requirements: Nextcloud Talk with a High Performance Backend, and a Korsi tenant with live meeting assistance enabled.
IMPORTANT: The environment variables below must be set in "Deploy Options", next to the "Deploy and Enable" button, before installing. The app refuses to enable without them rather than starting up and silently recording nothing.
info.author: Anupam Kumar
Marcel Klehr
Korsi

variable.name: LT_HPB_URL
variable.description: URL of the high-performance backend, same as the URL in the admin settings of Talk. It ends in "/spreed" usually and looks something like "wss://cloud.example.com/standalone-signaling/spreed".

variable.name: LT_INTERNAL_SECRET
variable.display-name: Internal secret of the high-performance backend
variable.description: Internal secret used to authenticate with the high-performance backend. This is the internal secret from the HPB and not the shared secret entered on the Nextcloud Server in the admin settings of Talk. It is set as "internalsecret = ..." in the server.conf file of the Talk Signaling HPB.

variable.name: KORSI_API_URL
variable.description: Base URL of the Korsi API, for example "https://api.korsi.ai". No trailing path.

variable.name: KORSI_TOKEN_URL
variable.description: OAuth2 token endpoint of Korsi's identity provider, for example "https://auth.korsi.ai/oauth/v2/token". The bridge exchanges its client credentials here for an access token.

variable.name: KORSI_TOKEN_SCOPE
variable.description: The exact scope string Korsi provided, pasted verbatim. It carries three identifiers the token cannot work without: the Korsi API audience, the project-roles assertion, and this organization. Edited or shortened, the identity provider still issues a token and Korsi refuses every request.

variable.name: KORSI_SERVICE_KEY
variable.description: The JSON key document Korsi provided, on a single line. The bridge signs a short-lived assertion with it to obtain access tokens, so the private key never leaves this server. Korsi cannot show it again — ask for a new one if it is lost.

variable.name: SKIP_CERT_VERIFY
variable.description: When set to "true" or "1", certificate verification is skipped for the websocket connections to the HPB. For test deployments with self-signed certificates only.
